newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends down 56 cts at six-month low.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends down 56 cts at six-month low.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures last traded at a six-month low of $20.07 a barrel on Thursday on bearish U.S. stock data and selling in New York before the expiry of the March NYMEX crude contract, traders said.
IPE April Brent crude futures ended down 56 cents in thin volume in a retreat that was given late impetus by market-on-close selling from Wall Street, traders said.
That is the lowest the front month has traded since August 28, when it closed at $20.27 after touching a low of $19.95.

The contract had repeatedly tested $20.10 in choppy activity throughout the afternoon, breaching it briefly around 1830 GMT before recovering as traders bought the dips and raised the contract to around $20.20 for most of the last hour of business.

March gas oil futures settled $2.50 lower at $173.50 a tonne, $1.75 above the day's low, after opening at $176 and touching a high of $178. It was dragged down by weaker crude and a seasonal decline in the heating oil market.

NYMEX crude was down 84 cents at $21.95, as traders rolled positions out of the prompt month ahead of the March expiry amid bearish stock data showing growiung crude supply. API stock figures released late on Wednesday showed U.S. crude oil inventories rose by 3.12 million barrels last week.
